title: Zereshk Polo Morgh
subtitle: barberry rice with chicken
excerpt: Zereshk Polo Morgh is a Persian celebration dish of saffron-stained rice layered with tart dried barberries and served with braised chicken. The barberries jewel the golden rice with bright red flecks. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Zereshk Polo Morgh is the most popular dish at Iranian weddings and celebration meals. The barberry and saffron combination has been central to Persian cooking for centuries.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Braise the chicken a day ahead. Reheat gently while cooking the rice fresh.

glossaryTerms.definition: Dried barberries, small intensely tart red berries used widely in Persian cooking to add sourness and colour to rice dishes.
The Persian style of cooking rice in which ingredients are layered through the rice during the final steam, giving a mixed, jewelled result.

content.text: in this dish are sauteed briefly in butter and sugar before being layered through the rice. This turns a plain
into something jewelled and fragrant. The chicken is braised separately in saffron and turmeric. Serves 4.
Make the chicken braise first so it can rest while you cook the rice. Both elements can then be served together at peak temperature.

items.prepNote: steeped in 4 tbsp hot water, divided

content.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken thighs skin-side down for 5 minutes until golden. Flip and cook for 2 minutes more. Remove and set aside. Fry the onion in the same pan for 10 minutes until soft. Add turmeric, stir for 1 minute. Return chicken to the pan, pour in stock and half the saffron water. Cover and simmer over low heat for 35 minutes.

While the chicken cooks, parboil the rice. Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil. Add the rinsed rice and cook for 6 minutes until just barely tender outside but raw in the middle. Drain through a sieve and rinse with cold water.
Melt 30g of butter in the large saucepan over medium heat. Add 3 tablespoons of the parboiled rice to the base and press down gently. This is a simple base tahdig. Mound the remaining rice on top.

Melt the remaining 30g butter in a small pan over medium-low heat. Add the barberries and sugar. Stir gently for 2 minutes until they plump and glisten. Spoon the barberries over the mounded rice. Drizzle the remaining saffron water over the top.

Wrap the pan lid in a tea towel and cover the rice tightly. Steam over low heat for 30 minutes. Serve the rice on a large platter with the braised chicken arranged alongside. Spoon the cooking juices from the chicken over everything.

attrs.solution: Cook them very briefly and only over low heat. They need no more than 2 minutes in the butter. Adding them to the rice while still red preserves their colour.
The rice was overboiled before steaming. It should be slightly underdone at the parboiling stage. Rinsing with cold water after draining also helps keep grains separate.
Ensure there is enough liquid in the pan during braising. The stock should not evaporate completely. If it gets low, add a splash of water and reduce the heat further.

content.text: Zereshk Polo Morgh is the most recognisable Persian dish outside Iran. It appears at almost every celebration meal. Barberries grow wild in Iran and have been used in Persian cooking for over two thousand years. The saffron and barberry colour combination, deep gold and bright red, is visually distinctive. No other cuisine has this exact combination.
